Voice AI startup ElevenLabs reportedly seeking new funding at $33B valuation
by Maria Deutscher
Artificial intelligence developer ElevenLabs Inc. is reportedly in early talks to raise capital at a $33 billion valuation.
Bloomberg today cited sources as saying that the company plans to close the round in the first quarter of 2027. According to the report, some investors are pushing for the raise to happen sooner. That hints the planned round may include a secondary sale, a transaction that enables existing investors to cash out their shares.
It’s unclear how much ElevenLabs hopes to raise or from whom. Late-stage startup investments almost always include contributions from existing backers. ElevenLabs’ most recent raise, which valued it at $22 billion, saw the participation of Nvidia Corp.’s NVentures fund, Blackrock, Wellington and several others.
ElevenLabs’ fundraising push reportedly comes amid a surge in customer demand. Its annualized revenue is said to have grown by $100 million since September, to $700 million.
Founded in 2022, ElevenLabs develops a series of AI models optimized to process audio. Companies use them to field call center inquiries, transcribe meetings, generate music and perform related tasks. It also offers a service called Productions that delivers ready-to-use audio assets.
The company debuted its newest and most capable model, Eleven v4, in late September. The algorithm’s flagship feature is its ability to tailor its speaking style to each text snippet. It does so by automatically tuning parameters such as tone and pacing.
Users can manually customize Eleven v4’s speaking style by adding instructions to scripts. They can also generate conversations with multiple synthetic speakers. A real-time version of the model, Eleven v4 Turbo, generates audio with only 150 milliseconds of latency for use cases such as customer support.
ElevenLabs offers Eleven v4 alongside more narrowly focused models. In May, it introduced an algorithm specifically optimized to dub videos. Additionally, it provides developer tools that make it easier to integrate its AI models into enterprise applications.
It’s possible ElevenLabs is raising new capital to finance more acquisitions. Earlier this month, it agreed to buy Kotoba Inc., a startup that develops audio processing models for companies in Japan. Nikkei Asia reported that the deal is worth $100 million. ElevenLabs will hire more salespeople in Japan over the next few months to grow its market presence.
A few days before the acquisition, ElevenLabs chief executive Mati Staniszewski stated that the company plans to start preparing for an initial public offering in 2028. That time frame suggests the round the software maker is currently raising could be followed by additional venture investments.

candidates.title: AI creative platform Evoken secures $200 million in new funding, valuation rises to $3.2 billion
candidates.snippet: AI creative platform Evoken secures $200 million in new funding, valuation rises to $3.2 billion KuCoin
candidates.text:
Dynamic Beating AI News: According to an exclusive report by LatePost, Evoken, the parent company of AI creative platforms Liblib, Lovart, and LibTV, has completed a new funding round of nearly $200 million, bringing its post-money valuation to $3.2 billion, with ongoing negotiations for a higher valuation. In June, Evoken disclosed a $300 million B+ round led by Granite Asia, Tencent, and Shunwei Capital, with a post-money valuation of $2.05 billion. In August, Bloomberg reported that the company is advancing a new funding round with a valuation of approximately $3 billion and has initiated preliminary discussions regarding a Hong Kong IPO.
The primary driver behind the valuation increase is LibTV, an AI video creation platform launched in March. LibTV integrates scriptwriting, storyboarding, video generation, and editing onto a single canvas, allowing users to freely access models from different vendors. LibTV has become the company’s largest revenue source, pushing the group’s monthly revenue to tens of millions of dollars.
However, this business previously had extremely low gross margins. According to data disclosed by Evoken to investors in July, the company’s overall gross margin for the first five months of this year was only in the low single digits, with model API procurement costs accounting for approximately 90% of operating expenses. The company’s annual procurement framework agreement with Volcano Engine alone exceeds RMB 100 million.
With the price reduction of Seedance 2.0 and the recent launch of lower-cost video models by MiniMax, Alibaba, and Keling, LibTV’s procurement costs are expected to decline. Some model providers are also beginning to rely on third-party platforms to acquire paying users. For instance, Sand.ai has chosen to exclusively release its latest video model, MAGI-2, via LibTV in China. One video model startup even revealed that over half of its revenue comes from third-party aggregation platforms rather than its own applications.

Israeli Chipmaker Altair Raises $100M in Series A Funding Round
By: Asia Business Outlook Team | Friday, 27 November 2026
Israeli semiconductor company Altair Semiconductor has raised $100 million in a Series A funding round to develop new chips and expand its connectivity business.
The investment was led by Maverick Silicon , the semiconductor investment arm of Maverick Capital, with participation from Israeli venture capital firm Pitango. The funding comes as demand increases for chips that help smart devices connect to AI services while using less power.
Altair plans to use the money to begin mass production of its ALT1550 modem in 2027, develop new products and expand its presence in international markets.
The company is focusing on products such as smart glasses, wearable devices and personal assistants that can connect directly to AI services without depending on smartphones for internet access.
Key Highlights
Israeli Chipmaker Altair Raises $100 Million to Expand AI Connectivity and Chip Production
Altair Secures $100 Million Series A Funding to Develop Next-Generation 5G Modem Technology
Altair Semiconductor Targets AI Wearables Market With $100 Million Investment and New Chips
Funding to Support AI Connectivity and Chip Production
The growing use of artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities for semiconductor companies . Technology manufacturers are working to bring AI features into everyday products, including smart glasses, wearable devices and personal assistants. These products need reliable internet connections to communicate with cloud-based AI services, but they also need chips that consume less power to protect battery life.
Altair aims to address this demand through its low-power cellular connectivity technology. Its upcoming ALT1550 modem supports several network standards, including 5G eRedCap , 4G Cat 1bis, LTE-M and non-terrestrial network connectivity. This allows manufacturers to use the same chip across different types of connected devices.
The company said the modem will help manufacturers move from 4G to 5G connectivity without making major changes to their existing product designs. It will also give device makers more flexibility when choosing processors for their AI-powered products.
Altair CEO Nohik Semel said connectivity will play an important role in the next generation of AI devices. He added that demand for the ALT1550 is higher than the company initially expected and that Altair is already working with device manufacturers on upcoming products.
Altair Focuses on Growth After Sony Spin-Off
The funding marks another step in Altair's journey as an independent semiconductor company. Sony acquired the Israeli chipmaker in 2016 for $212 million and operated it under the name Sony Semiconductor Israel. However, the Japanese electronics company later decided to separate the business as part of its restructuring plans.
Altair completed its spin-off from Sony Semiconductor Solutions in April 2026, following an initial $50 million investment led by Pitango Group. Sony retained a stake in the company after the separation. The move allowed Altair to operate independently and focus on its cellular Internet of Things (IoT) and connectivity businesses.
The company already supplies chipsets for several applications, including smart electricity meters, vehicle tracking systems, logistics equipment and wearable devices. These products use cellular networks to share information and send data to cloud-based platforms.
With the latest investment, Altair plans to expand beyond its existing markets and target the growing demand for AI-powered connected devices. The company is focusing on chips that can keep devices connected throughout the day without quickly draining their batteries.
The ALT1550 modem will be central to this plan, with mass production expected to begin in 2027. Altair also plans to build stronger relationships with device manufacturers and expand its customer base across North America, Europe and Asia.

The latest funding gives the company more resources to develop its technology and prepare for wider commercial operations. As AI features become more common in everyday devices, Altair is looking to strengthen its position in the semiconductor market by providing connectivity solutions for the next generation of smart products.

Scapia Secures New Funding Round to Support Growth and Innovation
Scapia has raised $63 million in a funding round led by General Catalyst , with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners and Z47 .
The fresh investment will support the company’s next phase of growth, strengthen its travel ecosystem and accelerate the development of AI-powered products and services for Indian travellers.
Scapia Focuses on Travel and Financial Services
Scapia operates at the intersection of travel and fintech, offering a travel-focused financial platform designed for consumers who frequently travel and use digital financial products.
The company combines travel booking services with financial products, creating an integrated ecosystem for discovering, planning, booking and experiencing travel.
According to the company, flight bookings on the platform have grown five to six times over the past year, while hotel stay bookings have increased eightfold. Growth has also been supported by rising demand from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities across India.
Funding to Strengthen AI Capabilities
A significant portion of the investment will be used to build an AI-first organisation and enhance the company’s technology capabilities.
The company plans to expand teams across:
Engineering
Product development
Data science
Design
Artificial intelligence
The company believes growing adoption of AI among younger consumers presents opportunities to create more personalised travel and financial experiences.
Investors Back Growth Strategy
Investors highlighted Scapia’s rapid customer growth and focus on travel-focused financial products as key reasons for supporting the latest funding round.
General Catalyst noted that changing travel behaviour among young Indians is creating opportunities for new consumer-focused businesses built around travel and lifestyle needs.
Existing investors Peak XV Partners and Z47 also reaffirmed their support, citing the company’s product innovation and execution capabilities.
New Products Expand Travel Ecosystem
Over the last six months, Scapia has launched several new offerings to strengthen its platform, including:
Scapia Pay
Rewards-based UPI services
Add-on credit cards
Credit card bill payment services
Scapia Store
Scapia Experiences
The company also allows users to earn and redeem Scapia Coins across travel-related services including flights, hotels, trains, buses, experiences and visa services.
Co-Branded Credit Card Portfolio Grows
The company offers co-branded credit cards through partnerships with Federal Bank and BOBCARD .
The company was the first in India to introduce a dual-network co-branded credit card operating on both Visa and RuPay networks.
It has also expanded airport-related benefits through its Airport Privileges programme, which covers dining, shopping and duty-free experiences in addition to traditional airport lounge access.
Travel Demand Continues to Drive Expansion
The company said growing travel demand among young Indian consumers continues to create opportunities for expansion.
The latest investment marks another step in the company’s efforts to build an AI-powered travel and financial platform for the evolving needs of Indian travellers.

The Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency launched a $50 million Atlantic Growth Capital Pilot at Sparta Manufacturing in Notre-Dame-de-Kent. Sparta also received $3 million from the Regional Economic Growth through Innovation program for a modernization project.
Why it matters
The pilot targets growing businesses that lack access to capital in Atlantic Canada, aiming to let companies expand while keeping their headquarters in the region. It follows a recommendation of the Atlantic Economic Panel for better access to expansion funding for businesses across New Brunswick and the wider Atlantic region.
The $50 million pilot offers repayable contributions starting at $2 million for businesses with at least $10 million in annual revenue, while Sparta's roughly $10 million modernization includes $3 million in ACOA repayable funding and $750,000 from a provincial MLA. How many firms will qualify and how quickly the pilot's funds will be committed has not been disclosed.
The players
Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency
A federal Crown agency that supports economic development and business growth across Canada's four Atlantic provinces.
Sean Fraser
A federal Member of Parliament and cabinet minister who represents a riding in Nova Scotia's Central Nova area and has been prominent in federal economic policy.
Benoit Bourque
A New Brunswick Member of the Legislative Assembly who announced $750,000 in provincial funding for the Sparta Manufacturing project.
The details
At the Sparta shop on Route 535, about 40 kilometres north of Moncton, officials announced the pilot alongside Sparta's modernization project, which includes a laser-cutting machine, a press brake and an automated system. Sparta Manufacturing, a Kent County firm that makes engineered-to-order waste processing systems, was founded as Allain Equipment Manufacturing in 1976 and employs more than 70 people. Businesses can submit expressions of interest from November 26 to December 11.
Timeline
November 26, 2026: Atlantic Growth Capital Pilot launched at the Sparta plant and expressions of interest open.
December 11, 2026: Deadline for expressions of interest to the pilot.
Season Trajectory
The pilot puts into practice a recommendation of the Atlantic Economic Panel to give growing firms better access to expansion capital so they keep their headquarters in Atlantic Canada. It marks a shift toward repayable, larger-ticket federal support for mid-sized regional manufacturers rather than smaller grants.
Eligible businesses with at least $10 million in annual revenue can submit an expression of interest to the pilot through December 11, 2026. Companies seeking expansion capital in Atlantic Canada may find repayable contributions starting at $2 million a more accessible option than before.
The takeaway
Growing manufacturers in New Brunswick now have a federal repayable-capital option sized to their expansion needs, so firms weighing a major modernization should review the December 11 expression-of-interest deadline early.
What happens next
Expressions of interest to the Atlantic Growth Capital Pilot close on December 11, 2026.

Hunt Capital Partners and Partners Close Financing for $22 Million Denton Supportive Housing Development
November 25, 2026
Hunt Capital Partners , O-SDA Industries and Denton Affordable Housing Corporation have closed financing for McAdams Haven, a planned $22 million supportive housing development at 1532 Bernard Street in Denton, Texas.
The project will include 84 furnished studio apartments in a four-story, elevator-served building. Homes will serve households earning up to 30%, 50% and 60% of area median income.
All apartments will be reserved for households with special needs, including people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, people with disabilities, veterans and survivors of domestic abuse. Referrals for households experiencing or at risk of homelessness will come through the local Continuum of Care or homeless service providers.
Half of the apartments will receive rental assistance through a project-based Section 8 contract administered by the Dallas Housing Authority.
Financing includes $20 million in federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Hunt Capital Partners, a $6 million construction loan from Bank OZK, a $919,000 construction loan from RAZA, a $6 million construction-to-permanent loan from the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs, and a $1.75 million Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas loan through Denton Affordable Housing Corporation.
“Having the opportunity to provide a safe and stable home for some of the most vulnerable members of our community is both an honor and a responsibility we hold very close to our hearts,” said Carrie Baugus , executive director of Denton Affordable Housing Corporation.
O-SDA Industries and Denton Affordable Housing Corporation are leading the development. Texas-based O-SDA specializes in affordable housing, while DAHC owns and manages 96 affordable units and has another 196 in development.
Hunt Capital Partners is the tax credit syndication division of Hunt Companies. Since 2010, it has raised more than $4.6 billion in tax credit equity through 55 funds, financing developments across 48 states and territories.

Leadership appointment follows TruDoc's $15 million Pre-Series B funding round
DUBAI, UAE , Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TruDoc Healthcare has announced Dr. Tarek Turk, MD, PhD, as Chief Executive Officer , following its $15 million Pre-Series B funding round and the milestone of serving more than 2.5 million lives over 15 years .
Since joining TruDoc in 2022, Dr. Turk has held senior leadership positions, including Product Owner, Chief Medical Officer, Chief Medical & Operations Officer, and Chief of Staff.
Continue Reading
TruDoc Names Dr. Tarek Turk, MD, PhD, as Chief Executive Officer
Driving the Next Chapter of Regional Growth
As CEO, Dr. Turk will lead TruDoc's strategic growth and operational expansion across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and wider global markets, with a focus on strengthening partnerships with governments, insurers, healthcare institutions, and corporate organizations. Central to his vision is the development of TruDoc's virtual-first healthcare model, which brings together primary care, chronic disease management, home diagnostics, pharmacy services, medical value travel and hospital-at-home solutions. He will also oversee the evolution of TruDoc's Super Health App.
A Leadership Appointment Built on Proven Experience
Commenting on the appointment, Vish Narain, Executive Chairman of TruDoc , said, " Dr. Tarek has been instrumental in shaping TruDoc into the healthcare organization it is today. He is more of a cofounder to this great company ."
Advancing a More Accessible and Connected Healthcare Future
Reflecting on his appointment, Dr. Tarek Turk, Chief Executive Officer of TruDoc , said, " I am honored to take on the role of CEO at such an important moment in TruDoc's journey. My priority is to build on the strong foundation we have established, deepen our partnerships across the GCC, and scale solutions that deliver sustainable improvements in patient outcomes and healthcare accessibility ."
A Distinguished Career Across Medicine, Research, and Digital Health
Dr. Turk brings more than 15 years of international experience. He holds a PhD from the University of Alberta, Canada , and a Doctor of Medicine degree from Damascus University . Prior to TruDoc, his professional experience included serving as an Advisor to the World Health Organization (WHO) in Switzerland, Senior Research Lead at the University of Alberta, Medical Director at Medicus AI, and Referee and Author for The Cochrane Collaboration in the United Kingdom.
About TruDoc
TruDoc is the region's largest virtual-first healthcare provider, dedicated to leading care beyond hospital walls.

Musk Wins Approval for 1 Million Satellites, Raising Sky Concerns
A long-exposure image of the Orion Nebula with a total exposure time of 208 minutes showing satellite trails in mid-December 2019. A. H. Abolfath/Wikimedia
This week, on the eve the Thanksgiving holiday, the United States Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX's plan to launch one million " Starmind " artificial intelligence (AI) data centre satellites. This decision reflects the convergence of a satellite boom, an AI bubble and the Trump administration's disregard for environmental regulation.
Author
Michael J. I. Brown
Associate Professor in Astronomy, Monash University
If Starmind proceeds in full, the number of operational satellites will be multiplied by a factor of 50. Space and our night skies will become vastly busier places.
SpaceX's pitch is to take the impact of data centres away from Earth, using a million solar-powered satellites to do AI data crunching in space and beam the results to Earth.
But what is the impact of one million satellites, both in space and on Earth? Why has the Federal Communications Commission made this decision? And will a million satellites actually end up in orbit?
Ups and downs
We are currently in a satellite boom, and constellations of hundreds or thousands of satellites are a key feature.
The Starlink internet satellites (another SpaceX project) is the best known example of such a constellation. Orbital rocket launches have increased to almost one per day , while the number of operational satellites is creeping towards 20,000 .
But Starmind represents something else. A million satellites.
To get so many satellites into orbit would be a vast undertaking. If the satellites have a lifetime of five years (similar to Starlink satellites), then roughly 500 satellites would need to be launched every day.
This also implies that roughly 500 satellites would eventually need to be disposed of every day. For satellites less than 2,000 kilometres above Earth, disposal usually means reentry and burning up in the atmosphere. And this has consequences.
When satellites burn up in the atmosphere, their materials react with and are deposited into the upper atmosphere. We now have satellites depositing far more aluminium, titanium, copper and lead into the atmosphere than the natural quantities from meteors.
Aluminium is of particular concern, as alumina can lead to the destruction of ozone in the upper atmosphere. This could increase ultraviolet light on Earth and the risk of skin cancers.
It's getting busy
Increasing the number of satellites by a factor of 50 is going to change our view of the sky.
If you look up during the early evening, you will see the stars your ancestors saw. But within a minute or two you will see a satellite. A point of light silently moving from horizon to horizon.
Our view of the night skies could fundamentally change.
Each satellite would be 75 metres wide and in the early evening they will be brighter than any star. And with a million satellites in orbit, there will be hundreds of Starmind satellites above the horizon irrespective of where you are.
The orbital clutter comes with real risks.
Satellites travel at speeds of roughly seven kilometres per second, and collisions produce clouds of debris that can produce further collisions. A nightmare scenario is the Kessler Syndrome - a runaway cascade of debris producing collisions that render low Earth orbit unusable.
Of course, SpaceX is aware of the risks of orbital collisions, and it already mitigates this risk with Starlink by manoeuvring satellites away from potential collisions. However, such manoeuvres require operational satellites and it is inevitable some satellites will fail.
Those uncontrolled satellites will pose a real danger.
Regulator or promoter?
The Federal Communications Commission has been a key regulator for American satellites. This has included regulating the radio frequencies that satellites use for communications to and from Earth, the disposal of satellites at the end of their useful lives and environmental impacts.
However, under the Trump administration, the commission is taking a looser approach to regulating satellites. This includes no consideration of environmental impacts, which is reflected in the FCC's decision on Starmind. It says the commission "will not require further environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act […] for SpaceX's Starmind system".
There are also some statements from the commission on Starmind that are, quite frankly, bizarre. For example, it claims Starmind "promises to bring the human race closer to a Kardashev II civilization - one that can harness the full power of the sun".
This is sci-fi silliness. A Kardashev II civilisation would need many trillions of square kilometres of technology in orbit around the Sun. Starmind is not a stepping stone to a vast " Dyson sphere " - a hypothetical megastrucutre that would surround the Sun and capture its energy.
But can it work?
One reason data centres are so unpopular on Earth is their use of precious resources, including water for cooling hot computer processors. But cooling in space is harder still. When stuck in a vacuum, one can only radiate heat away. And if you are familiar with vacuum flasks, you will know this can be a slow process.
Of course, it is possible to regulate heat in space, and satellites do it all the time. But they typically aren't pouring out heat like data centres do.
Google recently launched an AI demonstrator satellite into orbit and tasked it with undertaking AI calculations. But it had to have downtime between calculations to dispose of excess heat.
And apart from the physics there's the finance.
Right now we are in an AI boom, with the inflow of investment being vastly higher than revenues . And the cost of deploying AI in orbit will be vastly higher than equivalent AI on Earth.
